parts.article:
Dolls through the ages
 
(A) What is today a simple children's toy has a surprisingly rich history. Dolls have been a part of humankind for thousands of years. Often depicting religious figures, or used as playthings, early dolls were probably made from primitive materials such as clay, fur, or wood. Dolls constructed of flat pieces of wood, painted with various designs, and with 'hair' made of clay, have often been found in Egyptian graves dating back to 2000 BC. Egyptian tombs of wealthy families have included pottery dolls. Dolls being placed in these graves leads some to believe that they were cherished possessions. Girls from ancient Greece and Rome offered their wooden dolls to goddesses after they were too 'grown-up' to play with dolls. Most ancient dolls that were found in tombs were very simple creations, often made from such materials as clay, rags, wood, or bone. Some of the more unique dolls were made with ivory or wax. The main goal was to make the doll as lifelike as possible. That ideal led to the creation of dolls with movable limbs and removable garments, dating back to 600 BC.
 
(B) Following the era of the ancient dolls, Europe became a major hub for doll production. These dolls were primarily made of wood. Fewer than 30 examples of primitive wooden stump dolls from England survive today. The Grodnertal area of Germany produced many peg wooden dolls, a type of doll that has very simple peg joints and resembles a clothespin (a device for hanging washing on a clothesline). An alternative to wood was developed in the 1800s. 'Composition' is a collective term for mixtures of pulped wood or paper that were used to make doll heads and bodies. These mixtures were moulded under pressure, creating a durable doll that could be mass-produced. Manufacturers closely guarded the recipes for their mixtures, sometimes using strange ingredients like ash or eggshells. Papier-mâché, a type of composition, was one of the most popular mixtures.
 
(C) In addition to wooden dolls, wax dolls grew in popularity in the 17th and 18th centuries. Munich in Germany was a major manufacturing centre for wax dolls. Wax dollmakers would model a doll's head in wax or clay, and then cover it with plaster to create a mould. Then they would pour melted wax into the cast. The wax for the head would be very thin, no more than 3 mm. Some of the most distinctive wax dolls were created in England between 1850 and 1930. One of the first dolls that portrayed a baby was made in England from wax at the beginning of the 19th century.
 
(D) Around the same time, porcelain became popular. It is made by firing special clays in a kiln at more than 2372 degrees Fahrenheit (1300°C), and only a few clays can withstand firing at such high temperatures. Porcelain is used generically to refer to both china and bisque dolls; china is glazed, whereas bisque is unglazed. Germany, France, and Denmark started creating china heads for dolls in the 1840s. These china heads were replaced in the 1860s by ones made of bisque. Bisque, which is porcelain fired twice with colour added to it after the first firing, looked more like skin than china did. In France, the bébé was popular in the 1880s, and it has become a highly sought-after doll today. The bébé, first made in the 1850s, was different from its predecessors because it depicted a younger girl. Until then, most French dolls were representations of adults. Although the French dolls were unrivalled in their artistry, German bisque dolls became quite popular because they were not as expensive. Kammer & Reinhardt introduced a bisque character doll in the 1900s, starting a trend of creating realistic dolls.
 
(E) For many centuries, rag dolls were made by mothers for their children. The term 'rag doll' refers generically to dolls made of any fabric. 'Cloth doll' refers to a subset of rag dolls made of linen or cotton. Commercially produced rag dolls were first introduced in the 1850s by English and American manufacturers. Although not as sophisticated as dolls made from other materials, rag dolls were well loved, often as a child's first toy.
 
(F) Dollmaking did not become an industry in the United States until after the Civil War in the 1860s. Doll production was concentrated in the New England region of the United States, with dolls made from a variety of materials such as leather, rubber, papier-mâché, and cloth. Celluloid was developed in the state of New Jersey in the late 1860s and was used to manufacture dolls until the mid-1950s. German, French, American, and Japanese factories churned out cheaply produced celluloid dolls in mass quantities. However, celluloid fell out of favour because of its extreme flammability and propensity to fade in bright light.
 
(G) After World War I, dollmakers experimented with plastics. Hard plastic dolls were manufactured in the 1940s. They resembled composition dolls, but they were much more durable. Other materials used in doll manufacturing included rubber, foam rubber, and vinyl in the 1950s and 1960s. Vinyl changed dollmaking, allowing dollmakers to root hair into the head, rather than using wigs or painting the hair. Although most dolls are now mass manufactured using these modern materials, many modern dollmakers are still using the traditional materials of the past to make collectible dolls.

Q11 Dolls made of celluloid tended to lose their colour.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q12 Composition dolls lasted longer than the plastic dolls that were made in the 1940s.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE

reference:
Q1

干扰 题目中的 “used for the hair” 对应原文的 “'hair' made of...”，不要填 wood 或 designs。

句子 (Paragraph A) “...with 'hair' made of clay, have often been found in Egyptian graves dating back to 2000 BC.”

解析 题目说在埃及（公元前2000年），玩偶身体由木头制成，____被用于做头发，原文A段提到“with 'hair' made of clay（用粘土做的头发）”，填 clay。

Q2

解析 题目说古希腊罗马的年长女孩把玩偶送给____，原文A段说女孩们把木头玩偶“offered... to goddesses（献给女神）”，填 goddesses。

干扰 题目中的 “given to” 对应原文的 “offered... to”。

句子 (Paragraph A) “Girls from ancient Greece and Rome offered their wooden dolls to goddesses...”

Q3

解析 题目说公元前600年，逼真的玩偶有分开的衣服和可以摆在不同位置的____，原文A段提到玩偶有“movable limbs（可活动的四肢）”，填 limbs。

干扰 “Put in different positions” 对应原文的 “movable”。

句子 (Paragraph A) “That ideal led to the creation of dolls with movable limbs... dating back to 600 BC.”

Q4

干扰 “Became more common” 对应原文的 “grew in popularity”。

解析 题目说17-18世纪用____做的玩偶变得更常见，原文C段说“wax dolls grew in popularity（蜡制玩偶变得流行）”，填 wax。

句子 (Paragraph C) “In addition to wooden dolls, wax dolls grew in popularity in the 17th and 18th centuries.”

Q5

解析 题目说模具由____制成，原文C段说“cover it with plaster to create a mould（用石膏覆盖它来制作模具）”，填 plaster。

干扰 题目是材料介词 “made of”，原文是动作 “cover with... to create”，核心材料是 plaster。

句子 (Paragraph C) “...and then cover it with plaster to create a mould.”

Q6

解析 题目说1800年代一种被称为____的新混合物，原文B段中“'Composition' is a collective term for mixtures...（合成材料是混合物的统称）”，填 composition。

干扰 题目中的 “known as” 对应原文的 “collective term for”，这是专有名词，注意拼写。

句子 (Paragraph B) “'Composition' is a collective term for mixtures of pulped wood or paper...”

Q7

句子 (Paragraph D) “Bisque... looked more like skin than china did.”

干扰 “Looked more like skin” 意味着更真实（realistic），直接反驳了 “less realistic”。

解析 题目说素烧瓷（bisque）玩偶看起来比釉面瓷（china）玩偶“更不逼真（less realistic）”。原文D段说bisque“looked more like skin than china did（比china更像皮肤）”，即更逼真，选 FALSE。

Q8

解析 题目说法国玩偶往往比德国素烧瓷玩偶更贵。原文D段说德国玩偶变得很流行，因为它们“were not as expensive（没有那么贵）”，即法国玩偶更贵，选 TRUE。

干扰 原文是比较级逻辑：德国不那么贵 = 法国更贵。

句子 (Paragraph D) “Although the French dolls were unrivalled... German bisque dolls became quite popular because they were not as expensive.”

Q9

解析 题目说第一批布玩偶（rag dolls）是在1850年代制造的。原文E段说“For many centuries（许多个世纪以来）”母亲们就制作布玩偶了，1850年代只是“Commercially produced（商业化生产）”的开始，选 FALSE。

干扰 必须区分“first made”和“first commercially produced”，前者早得多。

句子 (Paragraph E) “For many centuries, rag dolls were made by mothers... Commercially produced rag dolls were first introduced in the 1850s...”

Q10

句子 (Paragraph E) “'Cloth doll' refers to a subset of rag dolls made of linen or cotton.”

解析 题目说只有用棉或亚麻做的玩偶才被归类为cloth dolls。原文E段明确定义：“'Cloth doll' refers to a subset of rag dolls made of linen or cotton”，选 TRUE。

干扰 原文用 “subset（子集）” 限定了材料范围，只有这两种材料才叫 cloth doll。

Q11

解析 题目说赛璐珞（celluloid）做的玩偶容易褪色。原文F段末尾提到赛璐珞失宠是因为极易燃烧和“propensity to fade in bright light（在强光下褪色的倾向）”，选 TRUE。

干扰 “Lose their colour” 就是 “fade” 的同义替换。

句子 (Paragraph F) “...propensity to fade in bright light.”

Q12

解析 题目说合成材料（composition）玩偶比1940年代的塑料玩偶更耐用（lasted longer）。原文G段说硬塑料玩偶“were much more durable（耐用得多）”比composition玩偶，题目说反了，选 FALSE。

干扰 比较级方向搞反是常见的错误陷阱，原文是塑料（latter）比合成材料（former）更耐用。

句子 (Paragraph G) “Hard plastic dolls... resembled composition dolls, but they were much more durable.”

Q13

解析 原文G段最后只提到现代制作者仍使用传统材料制作“收藏级玩偶（collectible dolls）”，并未提及收藏者是否偏好玩偶穿着“原装衣服（original clothing）”，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 文中提到了“collectible dolls”，但没有关于服装偏好的细节。

句子 (Paragraph G) “...many modern dollmakers are still using the traditional materials of the past to make collectible dolls.”
